## Solution

**Answer-leak check:** The problem statement contains only the system definition and instructions. No solution, sketch, or answer is embedded. Proceeding.

---

We solve $\dot{\mathbf{x}} = A\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{g}(t)$ with
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\-3&6\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{g}(t)=\begin{bmatrix}e^{-5t}\\4e^{-t}\end{bmatrix}.$$

### Step 1. Homogeneous solution — eigenvalues and eigenvectors

The characteristic polynomial is
$$\det(A-\lambda I)=(2-\lambda)(6-\lambda)+3=\lambda^{2}-8\lambda+15=(\lambda-5)(\lambda-3),$$
so $\lambda_1=5$, $\lambda_2=3$.

- **$\lambda_1=5$:** $(A-5I)\mathbf{v}=0\Rightarrow\begin{bmatrix}-3&1\\-3&1\end{bmatrix}\mathbf{v}=0\Rightarrow v_2=3v_1$. Eigenvector $\begin{bmatrix}1\\3\end{bmatrix}$.
- **$\lambda_2=3$:** $(A-3I)\mathbf{v}=0\Rightarrow\begin{bmatrix}-1&1\\-3&3\end{bmatrix}\mathbf{v}=0\Rightarrow v_2=v_1$. Eigenvector $\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\end{bmatrix}$.

Hence
$$\mathbf{x}_h(t)=c_1 e^{5t}\begin{bmatrix}1\\3\end{bmatrix}+c_2 e^{3t}\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\end{bmatrix}.$$

### Step 2. Particular solution via undetermined coefficients

Since $-5$ and $-1$ are distinct from both eigenvalues $5,3$, there is no resonance. We write
$$\mathbf{g}(t)=\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}e^{-5t}+\begin{bmatrix}0\\4\end{bmatrix}e^{-t}$$
and try $\mathbf{x}_p(t)=\mathbf{a}\,e^{-5t}+\mathbf{b}\,e^{-t}$.

Substituting into $\dot{\mathbf{x}}_p=A\mathbf{x}_p+\mathbf{g}$ and matching exponentials:

**$e^{-5t}$ terms:** $-5\mathbf{a}=A\mathbf{a}+\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}$, i.e. $(A+5I)\mathbf{a}=-\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}$.
$$A+5I=\begin{bmatrix}7&1\\-3&11\end{bmatrix},\quad \det=80,\quad (A+5I)^{-1}=\frac{1}{80}\begin{bmatrix}11&-1\\3&7\end{bmatrix}.$$
$$\mathbf{a}=-\frac{1}{80}\begin{bmatrix}11&-1\\3&7\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-11/80\\-3/80\end{bmatrix}.$$

**$e^{-t}$ terms:** $-\mathbf{b}=A\mathbf{b}+\begin{bmatrix}0\\4\end{bmatrix}$, i.e. $(A+I)\mathbf{b}=-\begin{bmatrix}0\\4\end{bmatrix}$.
$$A+I=\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\-3&7\end{bmatrix},\quad \det=24,\quad (A+I)^{-1}=\frac{1}{24}\begin{bmatrix}7&-1\\3&3\end{bmatrix}.$$
$$\mathbf{b}=-\frac{1}{24}\begin{bmatrix}7&-1\\3&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0\\4\end{bmatrix}=-\frac{1}{24}\begin{bmatrix}-4\\12\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1/6\\-1/2\end{bmatrix}.$$

### Step 3. Verification

**$e^{-5t}$ part:** $\dot{\mathbf{x}}_p^{(1)}=\begin{bmatrix}11/16\\3/16\end{bmatrix}e^{-5t}$, and $A\mathbf{x}_p^{(1)}+\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}e^{-5t}=\begin{bmatrix}-5/16+1\\3/16\end{bmatrix}e^{-5t}=\begin{bmatrix}11/16\\3/16\end{bmatrix}e^{-5t}$. ✓

**$e^{-t}$ part:** $\dot{\mathbf{x}}_p^{(2)}=\begin{bmatrix}-1/6\\1/2\end{bmatrix}e^{-t}$, and $A\mathbf{x}_p^{(2)}+\begin{bmatrix}0\\4\end{bmatrix}e^{-t}=\begin{bmatrix}-1/6\\-7/2+4\end{bmatrix}e^{-t}=\begin{bmatrix}-1/6\\1/2\end{bmatrix}e^{-t}$. ✓

### Step 4. General solution

$$\boxed{\mathbf{x}(t)=c_1 e^{5t}\begin{bmatrix}1\\3\end{bmatrix}+c_2 e^{3t}\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-11/80\\-3/80\end{bmatrix}e^{-5t}+\begin{bmatrix}1/6\\-1/2\end{bmatrix}e^{-t}}$$

where $c_1,c_2$ are arbitrary constants determined by initial conditions.
